$comment: Third-party semanticIds this crate is permitted to emit, plus a record of
every one we have ever tracked.
An entry in `allowlist` asserts, to a machine, that one of our fields means
what a standards body says its identifier means. That is a claim about
someone else's vocabulary, so it is only allowlisted once a human has read
the authority's own published source and recorded what they read.
Identifiers in the urn:odal-node: namespace need no entry — they are our
own concepts, honestly named, and the gate accepts them by prefix.
`allowlist` is currently EMPTY, and that is a deliberate state rather than
an oversight: this crate emits no third-party semanticIds at all. The claim
'AAS-shaped output carrying our own semantics' is thinner than
'IDTA-aligned' and it is true, which the previous claim was not.
`tracked` is the research record. Nothing in it is permitted — the gate
reads `allowlist` only, and a test asserts every tracked identifier is
refused. It exists so the next person who wants one of these starts from
what was found rather than from a search engine.

urn:samm:io.catenax.battery.battery_pass.licence: CC-BY-4.0 (verified 2026-07-31). Eclipse Foundation governance; no membership required to use the models, so referencing the identifier is permitted. Attribution obligations attach if the model's field definitions or descriptive prose are ever copied into our schemas — currently they are not.
verified: Exists: io.catenax.battery.battery_pass/6.0.0 is a real released aspect model.
Currency: 6.0.0 is current; 3.0.0 and 3.0.1 also exist.
notVerified: APTNESS — whether the Battery Pass aspect model actually describes the field set our BatteryTechnicalData submodel carries. This is the check that matters, and it was never done.
whyWithdrawn: A well-formed identifier naming the wrong concept fails OPEN: a consumer resolves it, receives a confident definition, and maps our fields onto it incorrectly, with nothing prompting them to ask. That is worse than a malformed identifier, which fails closed.

No Catena-X consumer exists in the picture to benefit, and the project has no association with Catena-X e.V. — which does not block use, since the model licence is permissive, but removes any reason to carry the risk.
Re-adding is one constant plus one allowlist entry, at the point where someone has a reason to do the semantic comparison properly.
urn:samm:io.catenax.battery.battery_pass.nextStep: Open the aspect model, compare its field set to BatteryTechnicalData, and if they correspond, restore the constant and add an allowlist entry with a named reader. Trigger: a counterparty already inside Catena-X asking for conformant output.

https://admin-shell.io/IDTA/02006/2/0.finding: Not IDTA's identifier form. IDTA semanticIds are name-based; this is the specification's document number transcribed into a URI, which nothing resolves.
https://admin-shell.io/IDTA/02006/2/0.alsoNote: The version referenced (2.0) is superseded — Digital Nameplate v3.0.1 is published.

https://admin-shell.io/IDTA/02004/1/2/Ma.finding: Document-number form again, with a '/Manufacturer' suffix that is our own invention rather than part of any published identifier.
https://admin-shell.io/IDTA/02004/1/2/Ma.correctIdentifier: unread — IDTA 02004 Handover Documentation, v2.0.1 published; open the specification for its declared semanticId

https://admin-shell.io/IDTA/02023/0/9.alsoNote: v0.9 is superseded — Carbon Footprint v1.0 (Mar 2025) and v1.0.1 are published. Adopt the current version, not this one.

https://admin-shell.io/IDTA/02011/1/0.finding: Two errors. Document-number form, AND our doc comment described it as 'Physical Properties' — IDTA 02011 is 'Generic Frame for Technical Data for Industrial Equipment in Manufacturing', a different template.
https://admin-shell.io/IDTA/02011/1/0.alsoNote: Check whether Technical Data is even the right template for material composition before adopting it — the original mapping may have been wrong about more than the URI.

urn:eclass:0173-1#01-AKJ975#001.finding: Two defects. 'urn:eclass:' is not an ECLASS-published URI scheme. And the Code Space Identifier is wrong for the use: in an IRDI 0173-1#0X-…, 01 denotes a Classification Class and 02 denotes a Property — this is a class identifier used as a Property semanticId, a category error even if the object exists.
urn:eclass:0173-1#01-AKJ975#001.correctIdentifier: unresolved — AKJ975 itself could not be looked up; the ECLASS dictionary needs portal access
urn:eclass:0173-1#01-AKJ975#001.nextStep: With ECLASS Advanced access, find the Property (02-space) IRDI for the EN 45554 repairability index specifically, not a generic score.

urn:idta:aas:submodel:digital-product-pa.finding: Coined, not looked up. No 'urn:idta:' scheme is in evidence anywhere; IDTA uses https://admin-shell.io/… URLs. This one carried no pin or warning comment, unlike the other six, so nothing marked it as unchecked.
urn:idta:aas:submodel:digital-product-pa.alsoNote: That is IDTA-02099-1, 'Digital Product Passport – Part 1: Metadata', implementing the EN 18223:2026 header fields. It is the closest thing to an official DPP submodel template and is worth revisiting deliberately — it may be the right identifier for our generic passport submodel.
